claims.text: The ladder mirrors :class:`daedalus.spine.cancel.ManagedProcess` exactly -- ``graceful`` via CTRL_BREAK to the process group, then ``tree_kill`` via ``TerminateJobObject``
claims.why: The class docstring makes a claim about the behavior of methods (graceful, tree_kill) that are not defined in this chunk; they are only described in the docstring but no code is present to verify.

claims.text: because the kill switch's sweep of last resort calls ``.cancel(grace_s=...)`` on whatever it finds and must not care which of the two spawn paths produced it.
claims.why: Refers to external kill switch behavior not present in this chunk.

claims.text: WHY A SECOND JOB-OBJECT IMPLEMENTATION EXISTS. ``ManagedProcess`` spawns through ``subprocess.Popen``, which cannot be given a token, so a Low child cannot come from it.
claims.why: Reference to ManagedProcess and subprocess.Popen not in this chunk.

claims.text: It is also slightly better: ``CreateProcessAsUserW`` hands back the initial THREAD handle, so the suspend/assign/resume sequence needs no toolhelp snapshot and has no window in which the child could spawn outside the job.
claims.why: Describes behavior of external code (CreateProcessAsUserW) not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The attestation for a run that could NOT be contained. Exists so the refusal path records the same shape as the success path; a result whose containment block is simply absent reads as "not applicable" when it means "we tried and failed".
claims.why: The function returns a ContainmentAttestation with contained=False, mechanism='none', and the given reason, which matches the description.

claims.text: Never the constants at the top of this file: those are what was asked for, and this dataclass only carries what was confirmed.
claims.why: References constants at the top of the file which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: A caller that records ``requested`` and calls it a security property has recorded an intention. The ledger gets this instead, so an attempt whose containment silently did not happen is visible afterwards rather than indistinguishable from one where it did.
claims.why: The dataclass includes requested, contained, and reason fields that allow distinguishing an attempt that failed from one that never happened.
